text:
Erik Karlsson is 36, still playing more than 23 minutes a night, and he's sitting in the middle of Pittsburgh's trade conversation. The Penguins have had a rough start, the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette handed him low first-quarter marks, and The New York Times has ranked him in its tradability tiers. Some of that is fair. Some of it is luck.

The fair part: Pittsburgh has been out-chanced with him on at five on five, 48% of the expected goals, and 7.4 points worse than without him. The luck part: the Penguins have scored 5.3 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, and he's pointless in four straight games despite 3.3 expected points in that stretch. He has 19 points in 23 games, 10 on the power play, which is a fine line for a down month.

Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd among defensemen last season with competition in the 97th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his shot assists in the 98th percentile. The playmaking is intact. Watch whether the bounces come back before the trade calls get louder.
